title: Business problem to Claude solution
task_statement: Turn a business request into a Claude solution with a stated outcome, constraints, and success criteria. (Inference: wording from secondary sources)

components.name: Use-case fit and lane choice
components.first_principle: Send fixed mapping to code and send open input to Claude only when a check in code can verify the output. (Inference)

nodes.label: Business request with outcome and constraints

steps: Write the outcome, the hard constraints, and the owner before you choose a model.
Sort each input type into fixed mapping or open input.
Send fixed mapping to code rules with no model call.
Send open input to Claude only when a code check can verify the output.
Set one metric and one threshold for each success criterion.
Name an owner who signs the result when the threshold fails.
pros: Fixed rules return the same output for the same input. (Inference)
Claude handles input whose wording and layout vary.
A code check limits the damage from a wrong model output. (Inference)
cons: The fixed path misses input types that no rule covers. (Inference)
Each path needs its own success criteria and eval set. (Inference)
use_when: The inputs vary, and a check in code can verify the output.
The task needs language analysis that rules cannot cover.
Several input types arrive in one queue.
do_not_use_when: The input follows a fixed format, and a rule covers every case.
No check in code can verify the output, and the error cost is high.
The team has no success criteria or eval set yet.

constraints.choice: Start with Claude Haiku 5.5, which the docs list for the lowest latency and price.
constraints.combination: Move to a larger model only when evals show a capability gap.

constraints.choice: Choose Claude Haiku 5.5 when the application needs low latency.
constraints.combination: Keep fixed steps in code when they need the lowest latency. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Use the Message Batches API for large volumes that do not need an immediate answer.
constraints.combination: Expect most batches to finish within 1 hour. A batch that does not finish within 24 hours expires.

constraints.choice: Name one owner for each success criterion. (Inference)
constraints.combination: Run the fit test again when the input mix or the error cost changes. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Write the lane rules with the team that owns the process. (Inference)

components.exam_tie: D1.1. Expect a business request with a cost or accuracy limit. The credited answer names the outcome, the lane, and a measurable success line. (Inference)
components.trap: A model call for a fixed format that a rule covers. It adds cost and a failure mode, and it gives no gain. (Inference)
components.decision_rule: Use code for fixed mapping, and use Claude with a code check for open input.
components.exam_tip: If the stem gives no success metric, add the metric before you pick the architecture. (Inference)

components.name: Success criteria and evals
components.first_principle: Write each success criterion as a measurable target with a threshold, and test it on an eval set before the build scales.

nodes.label: Eval set from real task inputs

steps: Write each criterion as a specific, measurable target.
Attach a threshold and a named owner to each criterion.
Collect test inputs that match the real task distribution.
Add edge cases, such as empty input and overly long input.
Grade outputs in code where possible, and use an LLM grader where code cannot check the output.
Compare each new prompt or model version against the same eval set.
pros: Automated scoring supports repeated runs on each change.
A measurable target shows whether a change helped.
Quality and operational metrics can share one report.
cons: Eval sets take time to build and maintain. (Inference)
Ambiguous cases split human graders, so the target needs a clear rule.
LLM-based scoring needs checks of its own. (Inference)
use_when: A team must decide whether to ship a prompt or model change.
A team compares two prompts or models on the same task.
An output that customers read needs a quality floor. (Inference)
do_not_use_when: The output has no measurable form, and no owner reads the result. (Inference)
The team needs a result for one demo with no users. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Run the eval set after each prompt or model change.
constraints.combination: Keep the eval set versioned with the prompt. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Name the owner who signs each threshold. (Inference)
Prefer more automated test cases over fewer hand-graded cases.
constraints.combination: Keep a small set of human-graded cases for calibration. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Use the Message Batches API for large eval runs that do not need an immediate answer.
constraints.combination: A batch that does not finish within 24 hours expires.

components.exam_tie: D1.1. Expect a stem that asks how to prove success. The credited answer names a measurable criterion with a threshold and an eval set. (Inference)
components.trap: A general quality goal, such as good performance. It cannot pass or fail, so no owner can sign it.
components.decision_rule: Write each criterion as a metric, a threshold, and an owner before you compare models.
components.exam_tip: If an option uses an adjective as the success test, prefer the option that adds a number and a test set. (Inference)

decision_flow:
flowchart TD
  A{Input varies in ways no rule covers?} -->|No| B[Fixed rules in code]
  A -->|Yes| C{Output checkable in code?}
  C -->|No| D[Redefine the task or add a reviewer]
  C -->|Yes| E{Criteria with threshold and owner?}
  E -->|No| F[Write criteria first]
  E -->|Yes| G[Claude with code check]
cheatsheet:
flowchart LR
  O[Outcome] --> C[Constraints]
  C --> F{Fixed mapping}
  F -->|Yes| R[Code rules]
  F -->|No| L[Claude with check]
  L --> M[Metric threshold owner]
  M --> E[Eval set]

patterns.wording: reduce cost for a task with a fixed input format
patterns.answer_type: code rules over a model call
patterns.rule: Use code for fixed mapping. Call Claude only for open input.
traps: Model call for a field that a rule reads

patterns.wording: success is described only with adjectives
patterns.answer_type: measurable criteria with threshold and owner
patterns.rule: Add a metric, a threshold, and a named owner before the build.
traps: More model tiers with no eval set
One demo result used as proof

patterns.wording: a wrong output reaches a customer
patterns.rule: Place a deterministic check between the model and the user.
traps: Prompt wording as the only control
Human review of every output with no check
